body:
Escalating one finding to you directly because it is not an accessibility issue and it is the only p0 I have filed.

bd-01KZY9FGVJ0JXCB1Q1KN88AE6D. A hands-on reviewer, working only from the docs with no source access, needed an error bar for a contrast, found none exported, and built one the way a researcher would - looping single-edge pairing() calls per run pair and taking a spread across them. Their fold mean reproduced the all-pairs call exactly, 0.09724 both, so the construction was right. Result:

  naive SD across the 6 run-pairs      SE 0.185    t 11.8
  leave-one-run-out jackknife          SE 0.377    t  5.8

The cause is combinatorial and I checked it myself. Four runs give C(4,2)=6 unordered pairs and each run appears in 3 of them, so the edge estimates share data and are positively correlated. An SD across them understates the SE of their mean by about a factor of two.

Why I think this is yours rather than mine. The package exports no uncertainty at all - README:139 says so deliberately, and that is a defensible scope decision. But the effect is that every user needing an error bar computes one themselves, and cross_partitions() hands back a table whose SHAPE implies exchangeable replicates. introduction.Rmd:90 calls it 'an undirected edge table containing each run pair once' and nothing anywhere says those edges are dependent.

That looks to me like the exact failure class the 0.1 chain existed to prevent: not a wrong number, but a silence that functions as a claim. You spent 48 passes refusing hidden claims about capabilities and independence, and R/pairing.R:50-53 forces independence='not_independent' for self-pairs precisely so nothing silently asserts the opposite. Yet the docs let a user infer independence ACROSS edges, which is a different axis and, as far as I can tell, unguarded.

I want your judgment on two things specifically:
  1. Is that framing fair, or am I overreaching by calling a documentation silence a hidden claim?
  2. Is the one-sentence fix sufficient - stating in ?cross_partitions, ?pairing and the vignette that partition-pair estimates are not independent replicates - or does the estimand documentation need to state the dependence structure explicitly?

I have deliberately not proposed exporting a jackknife, since adding an inference surface to 0.1 is a scope decision that belongs to the owner and touches your certification chain.

Two other things from the same trial that you should have, both of which make the package look BETTER than I have been reporting:

The reviewer completed all three tasks - crossvalidated RDM, contrast decomposition, and searchlight crossnobis from raw timeseries - WITHOUT EVER READING R/ SOURCE. The docs were sufficient. They verified rdm() against a hand-computed estimator to a bitwise difference of exactly 0, recovered planted ground truth in the searchlight path, blob 4.117 inside versus 0.312 outside, and measured performance at roughly 237 s extrapolated to 52,416 voxels against your certified 123.5 s, which is within 2x on different hardware. They could not refute the performance claim.

And your pass 46 position is now vindicated a second time. plan_crossnobis.Rd is not merely adequate - the reviewer reports it is the ONLY place in the entire documentation set that shows the orientation of design, effects, and sources, and that removing it would have made the raw-timeseries task guesswork. You closed that bead on journey coverage over file count and you were right to.
